title: POC scoping - open models shortlist & benchmarks
meeting_header: 2026-04-14 15:00 PDT | Duration: 52m | Redwood: Maya Chen, Owen Park | Sylph Tech: Rina Shah, Diego Morales, Priya Kapoor, Liam O'Connor
summary: POC scoping to select an open-model shortlist for a 6-week POC focused on multilingual customer support summarization and classification for financial product support. Discussed success criteria (latency, quality, cost), workload sizing (~20k daily chats, peaks ~200 RPS), benchmark plan (end-to-end latency + quality evals), and timeline. Agreed next steps: send model shortlist + perf matrix, run initial latency/cost estimates, customer to provide sample dataset and acceptance prompts, schedule infra deep-dive for private/VPC needs.
topics: Success criteria: latency, quality (ROUGE/QA/LLM evals), cost per 1M tokens
Workload sizing: 20k daily chats, peak 200 RPS, avg message 120 tokens
Model shortlist: open models tradeoffs (quality vs latency vs multilingual)
Benchmark plan: synthetic load + ground-truth quality evaluation
Deployment mode: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/private
Security/compliance: data residency, KMS, audit logs
transcript: [00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time today. quick intros?
[00:08] Rina (Sylph): Hi all, Rina here, head of ML. excited to scope this POC — we want to prove a multilingual summarization flow for support tickets in the finance product line.
[00:20] Diego (Sylph): Diego, eng manager, i'll be owning integration side and performance targets.
[00:25] Owen (Redwood): Owen from solutions. i'll be running the benchmark and helping with model selection.

[00:32] Maya (Redwood): Cool. quick agenda: clarifying success criteria, size of workload + traffic patterns, shortlist of open models with tradeoffs, and concrete benchmark plan + timeline. sound good?
[00:45] Liam (Sylph): yes, also a note on data privacy — Priya will chime in on what we can share for evaluation.

[00:51] Priya (Sylph): short version: we can share redacted transcripts and synthetic variants, but PII must be removed and we need an NDA addendum for any raw logs. we'll need KMS integration for any private deployment.
[01:10] Maya: noted. let's start with success criteria — Rina, what would make this POC a win?

[01:18] Rina: primary is quality first: summaries must preserve key entities and action items for compliance. we want >85% on our internal QA rubric and acceptable answer accuracy on a set of 800 eval queries. secondary is latency — for the summarization flow target is p50 < 150ms and p95 < 600ms end-to-end for single-turn summarization. cost target is under $X per 1M tokens — i'm not sure exact number yet, but we can discuss tradeoffs. and timeline: 6 weeks preferred to get to a decision.
[02:05] Owen: helpful. when you say end-to-end latency, is that the synchronous UI path?
[02:09] Diego: yes, user hits 'summarize', expect near-instant summary. we can accept async for heavy batches but the UI flow should be snappy.
[02:18] Owen: ok. workload sizing?

[02:20] Rina: rough numbers — 20k daily summaries, peak concurrency ~200 RPS for short bursts during business hours. avg message length ~120 tokens, average summary output ~80 tokens. we may have a smaller set of longer docs for contract summarization later — maybe 2k/day with much larger token sizes.
[02:45] Maya: good to know. that helps with batching strategy and model choice. next, model shortlist — Owen, can you run us through candidates?

[02:54] Owen: sure. since you asked for open models, our current shortlist is: Llama 3 70B (if available from OSS community forks), Mistral Instruct 70B, Falcon-180B (chat-tuned), Llama 2 13B quantized, and smaller Red-verified 7B chat variants. Tradeoffs: the bigger 70B class models tend to give higher quality on complex domain reasoning and multilingual coverage, but cost and latency are higher — even quantized they need careful GPU selection. Mistral tends to be strong on instruction-following and cheaper than some 70B alternatives. Falcon-180B can be good but historically has weaker non-English performance vs Llama variants. 13B quantized may meet latency and cost targets but might fail the 85% quality threshold on complex docs.
[03:45] Rina: multilingual is a hard constraint — we need good Spanish and French performance, and some German. how do these models compare?

[03:52] Owen: short answer: Llama-family (3 or 2) usually has decent multilingual coverage; Mistral has improved multilingual behavior in v2/v3 variants, but it depends on instruction tuning. Falcon historically weaker non-English. Our approach is to run a focused multilingual quality eval (samples in each language) as part of the POC. we can also use lightweight fine-tuning or instruction-tuning on redacted customer samples if needed.
[04:25] Diego: for the POC, will Redwood host the models or do we need dedicated infra?

[04:29] Maya: options: hosted API for fastest start, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, or Private/VPC for compliance. given Priya's note on KMS and NDA, we can start hosted with strict retention rules and redaction, but if you need KMS + no egress of logs we can plan a VPC pilot. typically we recommend starting hosted for the benchmark then shift to Dedicated or Private once you validate quality.
[04:58] Priya: short-term we prefer hosted with retention controls and SOC2 docs; long-term likely VPC with customer KMS.

[05:05] Owen: for benchmarking we'll measure three axes: throughput/latency under load, cost per token, and quality (ROUGE/QA metrics + human checks). we'll run synthetic load to validate p95 and qps and run your 800 eval queries across languages to score quality.
[05:25] Rina: can you baseline expected latency for each model — say a 13B quantized vs a 70B on an A100 or H100?

[05:33] Owen: rough numbers: 13B quantized on a single A10/A100 might hit p50 ~80-120ms and p95 ~250-400ms depending on batching; 70B on an H100 with optimized kernels could hit p50 ~120-200ms but p95 increases and batching decisions matter. Falcon or Mistral 70B also similar but cost varies. we'll provide a perf matrix with expected tokens/sec and cost estimates per model for your workload profile.
[06:05] Diego: we will probably want a production config that scales — what's Redwood's recommended autoscaling for bursts to 200 RPS?

[06:12] Owen: for 200 RPS with 120 token inputs, you'd likely want a small fleet of GPUs with concurrent model instances; exact numbers depend on model and batching. our Dedicated configs include autoscaling policies and warm pools to avoid cold starts; we'll propose a config after we run initial perf runs.
[06:30] Rina: quality evaluation — you mentioned ROUGE but our internal rubric also includes entity preservation and action-item extraction accuracy. can Redwood plug those into the eval harness?
[06:39] Owen: yes. we can run your rubric as custom evaluation scripts. we ask for redacted ground truth labels and then run both automated metrics and a small human eval panel for edge cases.
[06:50] Maya: let's talk deliverables and timeline. you're looking at a 6-week POC — how do we break that out?

[06:56] Rina: ideally week 0-1 data prep + model shortlist selection, week 2 perf runs and latency/cost estimates, week 3-4 quality evaluation and iteration, week 5 integrate real infra, week 6 decision + ops handoff.
[07:10] Owen: that matches how we usually run it. we'll aim to send the model shortlist + perf spreadsheet within 2 business days and start perf runs once you provide the sample dataset (redacted).
[07:22] Priya: timeline sounds ok but we need the NDA addendum before sharing redacted logs. we'll send legal comment by EOD tomorrow.

[07:30] Maya: noted. on benchmarks, we recommend a 3-stage test: small-scale local quality tests, a 48-hour throughput soak under synthetic load to measure tail latency, and a 1-week mixed workload run against your redacted dataset to capture multi-language coverage and edge cases.
[07:50] Diego: for the 48-hour run do we need to set up our infra or can Redwood host?

[07:55] Owen: Redwood can host initial perf runs on hosted clusters; if you want dedicated hardware or to run inside your VPC we can supply an infra spec and our infra team will collaborate to set up the dedicated pool.
[08:09] Liam: what about quantization? you mentioned quantized 13B — we saw artifacts in hallucination with heavy quantization in other experiments.

[08:16] Owen: good call. quantization reduces size and inference cost but can impact accuracy. for summary/high-precision tasks we test FP16 and 4-bit quantization variants and surface any drop in metrics. if quantized model fails the QA threshold we'll recommend a hybrid: smaller model for short replies and larger model for complex docs or a reranking flow.
[08:40] Rina: reranking could help — run a cheap model for candidate generation then rerank with a stronger model for high-value items.
[08:45] Maya: yep that's common. we can show cost math for a generator + reranker pattern during the perf spreadsheet.
[08:53] Priya: security checklist — we need SOC2, ISO27001, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration, RBAC, and audit logs. is that all standard?
[09:03] Maya: yes. we'll attach our security package and SOC2 report in the follow-up. VPC/private deployments support customer KMS and no-logs retention policies.
[09:12] Diego: any red flags on latency if we go VPC with cross-region? we prefer the VPC in same cloud region to avoid latency spikes.
[09:18] Owen: keep the inference region co-located with your users or edge — cross-region will add RTT. for strict p95 targets you want region-local clusters.
[09:25] Rina: ok. let's capture concrete next steps so we can move fast.

[09:29] Maya: i'll summarize now: 1) Redwood to send model shortlist + perf matrix and cost estimates by 2026-04-16. 2) Sylph to return NDA addendum + redacted sample dataset by 2026-04-20. 3) Redwood to run initial latency/cost estimates and propose Dedicated config by 2026-04-18. 4) schedule infra deep-dive for VPC/KMS with Priya and our infra team (target week of Apr 20).
[10:00] Priya: sounds good. legal will send NDA edits today.
[10:05] Maya: any other questions?

[10:08] Liam: just one — do you support mixed-precision pipelines where part of the model runs quantized and part runs fp16? we've seen some approaches where the attention layers are higher precision.

[10:18] Owen: yes in some runtimes we can do mixed precision or split model paths, but it's advanced and depends on the model architecture and deployment. we can explore if benchmarks suggest it's needed.

[10:27] Diego: on acceptance, the path is: meet the quality threshold on 800 eval queries across 4 languages and meet latency p95 target for UI flow on synthetic load. if both met, we flip to pilot and discuss commit for Dedicated capacity.
[10:42] Maya: perfect. i'll send minutes and attach the perf template. Owen will own the benchmark runs; Rina will own dataset and rubric. anything else?
[10:50] Rina: no, thanks everyone. excited to get started.
[10:54] Maya: thanks, will follow up with links. bye all.
[51:59] (call ended)
